title: Ember Peach BBQ Sauce
summary: A thin, pourable Ember sauce built on real peaches and honey — sweet, glossy, and made for brushing. Pairs with the Ember Peach Rub.
story: This is the pourable one — honey does the sweetening and the peaches do the talking. It cooks down just enough to come together, then gets blended smooth and finished with butter. Thin enough to brush on chicken and ribs, sweet enough to stand on its own as a dip. Pair it with the Ember Peach Rub for the full treatment.

items: 2 cups fresh or frozen peaches, pitted and diced

steps.title: Soften the peaches
steps.body: Simmer the peaches in a saucepan over medium heat until soft and breaking down, about 10 minutes. Mash with a spoon.

steps.title: Build the sauce
steps.body: Stir in everything except the butter. Simmer just 10–12 minutes — don't cook it down thick.

steps.title: Blend
steps.body: Blend smooth with an immersion blender.

steps.title: Butter finish
steps.body: Stir in the butter off the heat. If it's thicker than you like, thin with a splash of water. Cool and jar. Keeps 2 weeks in the fridge.

title: Ember Char Siu (Chinese BBQ Pork)
summary: Cantonese-style BBQ pork with a glossy red glaze — honey, hoisin, and five spice, finished over heat for those caramelized edges.
story: Char siu is China's answer to barbecue — pork marinated in honey, hoisin, and five spice, roasted until the edges char and the glaze turns to candy. The red fermented bean curd gives it that signature ruby color, but it tastes like char siu without it. Slice it thin over rice and you're in business.

items: 2 lbs pork shoulder, cut into long strips about 2 inches thick
2 Tbsp dry sherry (or shaoxing wine if you have it)
1 tsp red fermented bean curd, mashed (optional, for color — Asian market or online; skip it and it still tastes right)

steps.title: Marinate
steps.body: Mix all marinade ingredients. Coat the pork well, cover, and refrigerate overnight (at least 4 hours). Reserve 2 tablespoons of marinade before adding the pork.

steps.title: Cook
steps.body: Set the smoker or oven to 325°F. Lay the pork on a rack over a pan. Cook about 45 minutes, flipping once, until it hits 145°F internal.

steps.title: Glaze and char
steps.body: Boil the reserved marinade, mix with the honey, and brush over the pork. Cook 10–15 more minutes until the edges char a little.

steps.title: Rest and slice
steps.body: Rest 10 minutes, then slice thin against the grain. Serve over rice.

proTips.text: Everything here is in a regular grocery store except the red fermented bean curd — that's Asian-market or online only, and it's optional. Dry sherry stands in fine for shaoxing wine.

title: Ember Reverse-Seared Steak
summary: Thick-cut steaks cooked low and slow first, then seared screaming-hot — edge-to-edge pink with a dark crust.
story: Reverse sear is the pitmaster's steak method: gentle heat first for an even interior, then a hard sear for the crust. No gray band, no guesswork — just pull at 115°F, rest, and sear. The butter-garlic-thyme baste at the end is optional but you'd be a fool to skip it.

items: 2 thick-cut ribeyes or NY strips, 1½–2 inches thick
2 Tbsp Ember House Rub (or coarse salt, black pepper, and garlic powder)

steps.title: Season
steps.body: Season the steaks generously on all sides. Let them sit at room temp for 30–45 minutes (or salt the night before and refrigerate uncovered for a dry brine).

steps.title: Cook low
steps.body: Set the smoker or oven to 225°F. Cook the steaks until they hit 115°F internal for medium-rare — about 45–60 minutes.

steps.title: Rest
steps.body: Pull them off and rest 10 minutes while you get a cast iron skillet ripping hot.

steps.title: Sear
steps.body: Sear 60–90 seconds per side until crusty and dark.

steps.title: Baste
steps.body: Drop in the butter, garlic, and thyme — tilt the pan and baste for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Rest and slice
steps.body: Rest 5–10 minutes, then slice against the grain.

proTips.text: Pull at 115°F for medium-rare, 125°F for medium — the sear carries them up 10–15 degrees.

title: Ember Herb Compound Butter
summary: The butter everybody puts on steaks — garlic, parsley, thyme, and rosemary rolled into a sliceable log.
story: This is the stuff steakhouses charge extra for. Softened butter mashed with garlic and fresh herbs, rolled into a log and chilled — then you slice off a pat and let it melt over a hot steak. Also unreal on grilled chicken, roasted veggies, and a baked potato.

steps.title: Mix
steps.body: Mash everything together in a bowl until well mixed.

steps.title: Roll
steps.body: Scoop onto plastic wrap and roll into a log. Twist the ends tight.

steps.title: Chill
steps.body: Chill at least 2 hours until firm. Slice into pats as needed.

proTips.text: Keeps 2 weeks in the fridge, 3 months in the freezer. Slice a pat over a hot steak and let it melt in.

title: Ember Cowboy Butter
summary: The viral spicy butter — garlic, lemon, Dijon, cayenne, and herbs melted together. Made for dipping steak.
story: Cowboy butter broke the internet for a reason — it's garlic butter with attitude. Lemon and Dijon cut through the richness, cayenne and red pepper flakes bring the heat, and the herbs keep it fresh. Serve it warm as a dip for steak, chicken, or shrimp, or chill it and slice pats.

steps.title: Melt and mix
steps.body: Melt the butter and stir in everything until combined.

steps.title: Serve
steps.body: Serve warm as a dip — or chill, roll into a log, and slice pats like the herb butter.

title: Ember Garlic Parmesan Wings
summary: Smoked wings tossed in garlic butter and showered with parmesan — rich, savory, and dangerously easy to eat.
story: Garlic parmesan wings are the ones that disappear first at every party. Smoke the wings low for crispy skin and real smoke flavor, then toss them in garlic butter while they're hot so the parmesan melts right on.

items: 2 Tbsp Ember House Rub (or salt, pepper, garlic powder)

steps.title: Season and smoke
steps.body: Season the wings and smoke at 275°F for about 1.5 hours, until 175°F internal and the skin is crisp.

steps.title: Toss
steps.body: Toss the hot wings in melted butter and garlic, then shower with parmesan and parsley. Serve right away.

title: Ember Buffalo Wings
summary: Smoked wings tossed in classic buffalo sauce — the game-day standard, with real smoke under the heat.
story: Buffalo wings don't need reinventing — they need smoke. Cooking them low first renders the fat and crisps the skin, then the hot sauce and butter do the rest. Celery and blue cheese on the side, obviously.

items: 2 Tbsp Ember House Rub (or salt, pepper, garlic powder)

steps.title: Season and smoke
steps.body: Season the wings and smoke at 275°F for about 1.5 hours, until 175°F internal and the skin is crisp.

steps.title: Toss
steps.body: Whisk the hot sauce and melted butter together. Toss the hot wings in the sauce. Serve with celery and blue cheese.

title: Ember Honey BBQ Wings
summary: Smoked wings brushed with sticky honey BBQ glaze — sweet, caramelized, and gone in minutes.
story: Honey BBQ wings are pure crowd-pleaser. The glaze goes on in the last stretch so the honey caramelizes without burning. Sweet, sticky, smoky — the trifecta.

items: 2 Tbsp Ember House Rub (or salt, pepper, garlic powder)

steps.title: Season and smoke
steps.body: Season the wings and smoke at 275°F for about 1 hour 15 minutes.

steps.title: Glaze
steps.body: Whisk the glaze ingredients. Brush over the wings and smoke 20 more minutes, until 175°F internal and caramelized.

title: Ember Asian Sticky Wings
summary: Smoked wings in a sticky soy-honey glaze with ginger and sesame — sweet, savory, and finger-licking.
story: These are the wings that make people ask for the recipe. Soy, honey, garlic, and ginger reduce into a glaze that clings to every wing. Sesame seeds and green onions on top for the full effect.

steps.title: Season and smoke
steps.body: Season the wings and smoke at 275°F for about 1.5 hours, until 175°F internal and the skin is crisp.

steps.title: Glaze
steps.body: Simmer the glaze ingredients 5 minutes until slightly thickened. Toss the hot wings in the glaze.

steps.title: Finish
steps.body: Top with sesame seeds and green onions. Serve right away.

title: Ember Hot Honey Wings
summary: Smoked wings tossed in hot honey — sweet heat that builds. The wing everyone's talking about right now.
story: Hot honey is having a moment and wings are the perfect vehicle. Warm the honey with red pepper flakes so the heat blooms, strain it, and toss. Sweet first, heat second — that's the magic.

items: 2 Tbsp Ember House Rub (or salt, pepper, garlic powder)

steps.title: Make the hot honey
steps.body: Warm the honey with the red pepper flakes over low heat for 5 minutes. Stir in the vinegar, then strain.

steps.title: Season and smoke
steps.body: Season the wings and smoke at 275°F for about 1.5 hours, until 175°F internal and the skin is crisp.

steps.title: Toss
steps.body: Toss the hot wings in the hot honey. Finish with flaky salt. Serve right away.

title: Ember Pulled Pork Nachos
summary: Loaded nachos piled with pulled pork, melted cheese, BBQ drizzle, and jalapeños — the ultimate leftover play.
story: Pulled pork nachos are the reason to smoke an extra butt. Chips, pork, cheese, heat — layer it right and every chip is a loaded one. The trick is two layers of chips and cheese so nothing's naked.

items: ½ cup BBQ sauce, plus more for drizzling

steps.title: Layer
steps.body: On a sheet pan, layer half the chips, half the pork, and half the cheeses. Repeat.

steps.title: Bake
steps.body: Bake at 400°F for 10–12 minutes until the cheese is melted and bubbly.

steps.title: Top
steps.body: Drizzle with BBQ sauce and top with jalapeños, red onion, and cilantro. Serve right away.

title: Ember Barbecue Sundaes
summary: The Memphis classic: baked beans, pulled pork, and coleslaw layered in a cup with BBQ sauce on top.
story: The BBQ sundae was born at Memphis in May — beans on the bottom, pork in the middle, slaw on top, sauce over everything. Served in a clear cup so you see the layers. It's a whole plate of barbecue you can eat with a spoon.

steps.title: Layer
steps.body: In a clear cup or jar, layer beans on the bottom, pulled pork in the middle, and coleslaw on top.

steps.title: Sauce
steps.body: Drizzle BBQ sauce over the top. Hand them a spoon and stand back.
